purpose: Curated current primary-source records that must be merged into the relevant Mission Timers before publication. These records distinguish enacted law, active enforcement, technical rollout, privacy safeguards and bounded hypothesis.

records.title: Australia's under-16 social-media account restriction is in force
records.summary: From 10 December 2025, age-restricted social-media platforms must take reasonable steps to prevent Australians under 16 from creating or keeping accounts. The regulator reports that major platforms removed access to millions of under-16 accounts and continues compliance monitoring.
records.evidenceLevel: Official regulator · law in force · active compliance
records.identityLink: Platforms must operate age-assurance systems, but the legal obligation is on platforms and includes privacy restrictions.
records.claimBoundary: This proves mandatory age restriction and age-assurance deployment in Australia. It does not prove that the stated child-safety purpose is a covert digital-ID plan.

records.title: Australia updates the platform definition used by its social-media minimum-age law
records.summary: Australia updated the rules in March 2026 to focus the minimum-age obligation on account-based recommender systems and design features such as endless feeds, feedback signals and time-limited content.
records.identityLink: The regulated scope determines where platforms must deploy account-age controls.
records.claimBoundary: The update demonstrates continuing implementation, not a finding about hidden motive.

records.title: UK age checks are deployed at unprecedented scale under the Online Safety Act
records.summary: Ofcom's July 2026 statutory report states that many services are required to use highly effective age assurance and that age checks have been deployed at unprecedented scale. Ofcom continues enforcement and says the UK is preparing an under-16 social-media restriction.
records.evidenceLevel: Official regulator · statutory report · active enforcement
records.identityLink: Regulated services must determine whether users meet age thresholds using highly effective age assurance.
records.claimBoundary: This proves large-scale age assurance. It does not establish that every service must collect a government identity document or that a single universal identity database exists.

records.title: EU urges Member States to make a common age-verification app available by the end of 2026
records.summary: The European Commission adopted a recommendation on 29 April 2026 urging Member States to accelerate rollout of the EU age-verification app. The app may operate independently or be integrated into a European Digital Identity Wallet.
records.identityLink: The Commission explicitly permits integration with European Digital Identity Wallet infrastructure.
records.claimBoundary: Wallet compatibility is documented infrastructure convergence. It does not prove that child safety is merely a cover or that the wallet will become compulsory for all online activity.

records.title: EU age-verification blueprint is technically ready and supports national eIDs, passports and identity cards
records.summary: The Commission says its age-verification solution became feature-ready in April 2026. Proof of age can be issued from national eIDs, passports, identity cards, banking apps or offline activation, while the design aims to disclose only the required age threshold.
records.identityLink: The proof can be bootstrapped from government identity documents, national eIDs or existing trusted applications, while using selective disclosure and zero-knowledge techniques.
records.claimBoundary: The identity-document onboarding route is documented. The privacy-preserving design is also documented and must be included as counter-evidence against claims of inevitable centralised identity tracking.

records.title: Denmark, France, Greece, Italy and Spain are adopting customised versions of the EU age-verification solution
records.summary: The Commission identifies Denmark, France, Greece, Italy and Spain as Member States taking up the common technical solution with a view to publishing customised national age-verification applications.
records.evidenceLevel: Official EU rollout record · multi-jurisdiction adoption
records.identityLink: The national apps use a harmonised proof-of-age architecture designed to interoperate with European identity-wallet standards.
records.claimBoundary: Common architecture across several countries proves policy and technical convergence, not a secret unified identity mandate.

records.title: France enacted a digital-majority law requiring parental consent below 15 and certified age-verification solutions
records.summary: France's 7 July 2023 law requires social-network providers to refuse registration by children under 15 without parental consent and provides for certified technical solutions to verify age and parental authorisation, subject to implementing measures and European-law constraints.
records.identityLink: The law expressly requires technical age and parental-authorisation verification mechanisms.
records.claimBoundary: The statute is real, but its practical enforcement and compatibility with EU law must be tracked separately from the enacted text.

records.title: EU protection-of-minors guidelines and age-verification prototype establish a common DSA implementation route
records.summary: In July 2025 the European Commission issued protection-of-minors guidelines and an age-verification prototype under the Digital Services Act, creating a common compliance and technical route for platforms operating across the EU.
records.evidenceLevel: Official EU regulatory guidance · technical prototype
records.identityLink: The common prototype provides reusable proof-of-age infrastructure for platform compliance.
records.claimBoundary: The DSA route establishes common compliance expectations but the guidelines themselves do not prove a universal compulsory identity system.
